questions.heading: Only the Log Says Whether a Hint Was Used
questions.stem: A planner passes last quarter's plan as a complete hint to HiGHS, solves to optimality, and gets the same objective as the solve without a hint. What can the planner conclude about the hint?

options.text: HiGHS ignored it, since the objective did not move
options.says: A hint never changes the optimum of a solve run to optimality; every hint in lesson 4.3.3 gave the same NPV, used or not.

options.text: Nothing from the objective; HiGHS's log says whether it was used
options.says: Right: the optimum is the same either way, and lines such as 'MIP start solution is feasible' are the evidence.

options.text: HiGHS used it, since a complete hint is always taken as the start
options.says: A complete hint that breaks a rule is rejected ('cannot yield feasible solution'); only the log tells which happened.

options.text: The hint was infeasible, since a used hint makes the answer differ
options.says: A used hint changes the path to the optimum, not the optimum itself.

questions.heading: Filters Choose Which Values Come Back
questions.stem: A route model is solved with variable_values_filter=VariableFilter(skip_zero_values=True), and the result holds y_east = -2.2e-15 among its values. How should the code decide which routes run?

options.text: Every route present in the filtered values runs, since zeros were skipped
options.says: The filter skips exact zeros only; -2.2e-15 is round-off of 0 and was returned, as HiGHS did in lesson 4.3.3.

options.text: A route runs when its value is above 0.5
options.says: Right: binaries come back with round-off, so read them against 0.5, filtered or not.

options.text: A route runs when its value is not exactly 0
options.says: -2.2e-15 is not exactly 0, so this would run a route the plan does not use.

options.text: A route runs when its value is above 0, since negative values were skipped
options.says: skip_zero_values skips only exact zeros; y_east = -2.2e-15 is still in the result, and a tiny positive value would pass a > 0 test too.

questions.heading: An LP Starts From a Basis, Not a Hint
questions.stem: A nightly job solves a large LP with GLOP and stores the result. The next night one budget changes, and a new process solves again. What gives the new solve the best start?

options.text: A SolutionHint holding yesterday's variable values
options.says: The SolutionHint docstring says simplex solvers prefer a basis; a hint must first be converted into one.

options.text: A new IncrementalSolver created in the new process
options.says: A new IncrementalSolver starts from nothing; it only helps across solves in the same live solver.
Right: a stored basis can start any later solve; GLOP needed 32 iterations from it against 338 cold.

options.text: Nothing, since GLOP starts every solve from scratch whatever it is given
options.says: Given yesterday's basis, GLOP's iterations fell from 338 to 32.
